items.title: Signed-in shopper clicking footer "Track an order" lands on My orders
covers: Expected: Track an order opens the My orders page (/user/orders)
items.reason: This is the bug's reproduction and the acceptance criterion verbatim: the link had no destination, so a click did nothing. It must be e2e because the defect is a rendered anchor in the WebApp footer and the outcome is browser navigation to an authorized page; no cheaper layer renders the footer and follows the link.

items.title: "Track an order" and "My orders" footer links resolve to the same destination
covers: Expected: the same page as the footer's "My orders" link
items.reason: The Expected result ties the fix to the existing "My orders" footer link, not just to a path string. Comparing the resolved `href` of both rendered anchors guards against a near-miss (absolute vs relative path, typo, extra query) that would still differ from "My orders". It is e2e because only the rendered page resolves the relative `href` against the app's base URL.

items.title: "Track an order" keeps its text and third place in the Support column
covers: Expected: the link text and its place in the footer are unchanged
items.reason: The Expected result explicitly forbids moving or relabelling the link while fixing it (for example merging it into "My orders" or moving it to Shop). Asserting the Support column's ordered link list on the rendered page is the only way to see what the shopper sees, hence e2e.

items.title: Every other footer link is unchanged
covers: Expected: every other footer link is unchanged
items.reason: The Expected result requires the fix to touch only "Track an order". The regressions it guards against are giving placeholder links destinations, removing links, or changing existing destinations. The baseline below is the footer as it is on `main` (`src/WebApp/Components/Layout/FooterBar.razor`); it is checked on the rendered page, so e2e.

items.title: Anonymous click on "Track an order" is sent to sign-in, exactly like "My orders", and shows no orders
covers: Expected: the same page as the footer's "My orders" link
Bug Report: the orders a signed-in shopper can track are on My orders
items.reason: The story says the trackable orders belong to a *signed-in* shopper and that "Track an order" must open the same page as the footer's "My orders" link. For an anonymous visitor that page (`/user/orders`, `[Authorize]`) demands sign-in, so the fixed link must behave exactly like "My orders": challenge for sign-in and never show an orders page without an identity. The risk is a fix that points somewhere unprotected or different from "My orders". The expected outcome is defined by comparison with "My orders" rather than by an invented error body; it is e2e because only the running WebApp and Identity produce the challenge redirect.

The signed-out case only asserts parity with 'My orders' and the unstated behaviour is listed under Open questions; seeded user, page and footer section are all named precisely.
